keyVerseText: So shall my righteousness answer for me in time to come, when it shall come for my hire before thy face: every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and brown among the sheep, that shall be counted stolen with me. in time: Heb. to morrow
rootMeaning: The Hebrew verb גָּנַב (gânab) is a primitive root that fundamentally conveys the action of carrying away or taking something secretly. Beyond the common English gloss of 'steal,' its root sense emphasizes the clandestine nature of the act—removing or obtaining something by stealth rather than open force. This nuance highlights not only the physical act of theft but also the underlying intent to deceive or hide the action, which enriches our understanding of the term in biblical contexts.
usageInScripture: With approximately 40 occurrences in the Hebrew Bible, גָּנַב consistently appears in contexts involving the act of stealing or being stolen from. The top translations such as 'had stolen,' 'steal away,' and 'stole away' demonstrate a range from literal theft to idiomatic expressions of secret removal. This consistency reveals the word’s primary focus on stealth and deception, whether in physical theft or metaphorical senses, underscoring its broad application in Scripture to both tangible and intangible forms of taking or losing.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding גָּנַב in its original sense is vital for grasping the biblical view of sin and human brokenness. Theft, as an act done secretly and deceptively, mirrors humanity's fallen nature—seeking to take what is not rightfully theirs and doing so under cover. This verb thus points to the deeper spiritual reality of sin as both a hidden and harmful force. Christ’s redemptive work confronts this reality by exposing and overcoming deception and theft, restoring what was lost and calling believers to live transparently and justly before God and others.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 30:33 says, 'every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and brown among the sheep, that shall be counted stolen with me.' Here, the use of גָּנַב signifies that the unmarked animals will be considered as having been stealthily taken or wrongfully acquired. This highlights the importance of rightful ownership and integrity in God’s covenantal dealings and illustrates how the concept of theft extends beyond mere physical taking to include what is counted or accounted as taken, reinforcing the seriousness of honesty and righteousness in God’s eyes.
